convoLines.text: "I can't reach this properly. Could you clean it out for me? Please."
"It's getting worse, not better. If it festers I'm no good to anyone — can't haul, can't hunt, can't watch. Just clean it out and wrap it tight."
Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Saw things with too many joints. Give them room. That's the whole lesson."
There — the story splits again. You mark the spot.
"You're a good listener, you know that?" A tired smile.
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"...Okay. I'll figure it out." They won't ask twice. That much is clear.
Another crack. The telling doesn't hold together anymore.
The ground remembers.
Names, named.
"I should go. You know where to find me."
"Okay. I'll manage on my own."
"Are you going to stay? With us. For real. …sorry."
Something eases in their shoulders. "Good. We're better with you here. I mean that."
"There's more, but that's for another fire."
You watch who eats with whom, who laughs a little too loud at whose jokes. Nothing solid. Keep looking.
You say nothing. The silence sits at the fire with everyone else.
The moot is called. The fire gets built up.
Counted.
The ground remembers.
"I should get back to it."
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"You said you're staying — you didn't expect to say it, but you said it. Still true?"
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
A flicker at the corner of their mouth. Not quite a smile. Not quite anything.
"I wasn't a baker. I was a line cook. You don't know what it's like, being the only nobody in a camp of somebodies."
"That again?" Aurora sighs. "I confessed that already. I'm not confessing it twice for dramatic effect."
Aurora looks at you, level. "I told you the truth. You can keep poking it, but it's told."
"Still on that personal stuff."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
You show them Staghorn Sumac — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Alright. Catch you later."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"This was good." They mean it.
"Have you ever hurt someone? Since all this started. That's my read."
They nod, slow. "Okay. Thank you for telling me. That couldn't have been easy to say."
"Still on whether you've hurt someone."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"Walk my trap line with me? Extra hands, extra eyes."
Linh shows you where they go to think. "Don't tell the others. Everyone needs one place."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Skylar owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
"I keep turning over the last thing Skylar said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
"Let me sit with all that. We'll pick it up later."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"You told me yes, once. No details. I haven't forgotten. I just don't ask."
Linh has an edge today — something curdled.
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on that personal stuff."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"Yeah? What's up?"
"Good question." "Last time things were different. They always are." "They took me. Pattern Hunger — up there, on the screens, in front of everyone. I'm still turning it over."
"I do the small things right. The big things notice."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"This was good." They mean it.
"We never did finish talking about that favor — that was 11 days back. Still on your mind? 'I should go. You know where to find me.'"
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
The easy manner evaporates. What's left is watching you back.
*You've pulled a confession before — they come when the evidence is heavy. One thread isn't a rope.*
"You know what, fair." Marcus nods slowly. "I can see how that looked. But here's the thing..." And the thing is mundane, and verifiable, and fine.
Something crosses their face — quick, then gone. The practiced expression clicks back into place.
*Confessions need weight behind them. What you have right now is a thread. Find the rope.*
"Wait, wait —" Marcus holds up a hand, smiling. "I can see exactly why that sounded wrong. No — it's like this..." The pieces slot into place. Of course.
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Huh. I wouldn't have guessed that about you."
"Still on that question."
"Right. Action time. You know where to find me."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"I'm not sure, but What are you hoping for? Not the big stuff. The small thing."
"Okay." Something shutters, just slightly.
"Still on what you're hoping for."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"

"Huh. Let me think about that." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "You want to know what I did in the raid? I stood down The Big Beast at the treeline — it ran. Don't call it brave. Call it awake."
"That's the whole of it. Sorry."
They fill the quiet. "Anyway — where was I?"
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Alright — carefully, now. Both of us."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Can I tell you something? I'm keeping a photo of someone I left behind. I haven't told anyone."
"There's more, but that's for another fire."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on their secret."
"...Anyway. What did you want to ask?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "That night — I stood down Lockpick at the treeline — it ran. I keep hearing it when I try to sleep."
"I sharpen sticks down to nothing when it gets loud in my head. The treeline gets loud in my head."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Alright — I should get back to it."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"We're eating through stores faster than we replace them. Forage with me tomorrow? I know the ridge above the creek."
"The stores won't stretch past tomorrow, and I'm not choosing who eats. I know the ridge above the creek — come with me and we'll fill packs before dark."

"Still on what's been happening."

"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
"This was good." They mean it.
"The pantry's nearly bare. Will you forage with me tomorrow? Two pairs of eyes, twice the ground."
"Another day like today and we're choosing who eats. Meet me at where the giant water lily grows thick and we'll fill packs before dark."

"Someone has to show the new folks where the door IS. That's me now, I guess."

"Still on what's been happening."

deathBeat: d13: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Skylar Villanueva is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d13: 🕯️ Skylar Villanueva is dead — the arena. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d13: The village's quarrel was with Skylar — and Skylar is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
d15: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Hushpuppy is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
recoverHome: d14: That night, they bring Skylar home. Nobody asks you to help carry; nobody has to. By morning the grave is dug by the fire, and the body is laid out beside it. The filling of it is yours.
systemVoice: d13: SYSTEM: "Perimeter violated! This is unprecedented! ...Is this unprecedented? Checking. Yes. Unprecedented."
d13: SYSTEM: "INTRUDER REPELLED. The pantry’s aroma is now classified as a defensive liability. The audience is chanting the defenders’ names. Fan clubs are forming. This is how it starts."

d13: ◈ ARC III — ENGINES. SYSTEM: "VIEWERSHIP MILESTONE. Organic unit demonstrates compounding capability. Resonance protocols unlocked." — Your gifts deepen. Used in sequence, they resonate. The village is no longer just surviving. It is becoming something.
d13: ⬢ SYSTEM: "Neural depth 50. I can hold more of you now — ability slots: 4."
d14: 📺 SYSTEM: "AUDIENCE EXPANSION! Your party cap is now FOUR! The people demanded bigger ensembles! Don't let us down!"
d14: 📺 SYSTEM: "A viewer sent this. A FAN. We checked. It is not dinner." A pause. "We checked twice. The fans are very insistent that you open it ON CAMERA."
d14: SYSTEM: Oh! It has a NAME. You all love names.
d15: ◈ SYSTEM: "PALISADE: ONLINE. Pointy! The audience approves of pointy. Raiders will think twice — the ones that can think. Sleep easy, little ones. The walls are watching so you do not have to."

d15: ◈ SYSTEM: "The long game, little hoarders. A GRANARY. Stockpile 20,000 kcal, 500 wood and 2,000 kcal of PRESERVED food — food that WAITS. Smoke it, dry it, render it. The audience finds delayed gratification EXOTIC. So do stomachs, we are told."

d20: "I keep turning over the last thing Skylar said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."

lastSay: d58: — DAY 58 DAWN — The world wakes. Animals are active.
d58: Overnight, Wild Onion went bad — beyond saving. You leave it for the flies.
d58: Fresh food keeps days, not weeks. Smoke it over a fire to make it last.
